citation.authors: Kim In-Sook, Park Soo-yeon, Park Min Ju, Kim Kyeong Jin, Kim Ji Yeon
citation.title: Effect of Barley on Postprandial Blood Glucose Response and Appetite in Healthy Individuals: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial

population.description: Healthy adults aged 20 to 65 with fasting glucose below 126 mg/dL, with active disease and other exclusions screened out (Methods 2.3); 70 participants at baseline (Table 1), 67 completed both visits. Age and BMI are Table 1 means with SE, converted to SD as SE x sqrt(70): 1.1 x 8.37 = 9.2 and 0.4 x 8.37 = 3.35; min and max are not printed. Sex from Table 1: 55 male, 15 female.

protocols.name: placebo_drink
protocols.description: Rice-flour placebo product (150 g in 500 mL water, Methods 2.1 and 2.5) with a 30 g glucose load (Methods 2.5 and 2.6: 'after consuming either the BDF or placebo product with 30 g of glucose loading'), drunk at minute 0 after a fast of at least 12 h. Printed (Methods 2.1): placebo 'provided a total of 539.36 kcal per 150 g serving ... 90.2% energy from carbohydrates (121.6 g), 7.5% from protein (10.1 g), and 2.3% from fat (1.4 g)'; 'The carbohydrates in the placebo product included 0.4 g of fiber'. Derived: carbs_g of the product = 121.6 - 0.4 = 121.2 (total carbohydrate less printed fibre), plus the 30 g glucose = 151.2. fibre_g 0.4, fat_g 1.4, protein_g 10.1 as printed. Samples: 0 min (fasting, before the drink), then 30, 60, 120, 180 min after consumption (Methods 2.5). Clock hour not stated (start_hour 8.0 assumed). Whether the glucose was dissolved in the drink is not stated; it is entered as one meal at minute 0. The barley-fibre arm is not entered (see left_out).

meals.food: rice flour drink with 30 g glucose

findings.description: Plasma glucose after the placebo drink with 30 g glucose, mean and SE at 0 to 180 min (placebo column of Table 2; Methods: 'The results are presented as the means ± standard errors'). Table 2 prints no n; 67 is the number who completed both visits (33 + 34 after 3 withdrawals, Results 3.1; Abstract 'n = 67'), used for every Table 2 and Results-text value.

location.where: Table 2, 'Blood glucose (mg/dL)', Placebo column, rows 0 to 180 min

Table 2 prints no n; 67 is the number who completed both visits (33 + 34 after 3 withdrawals, Results 3.1; Abstract 'n = 67'), used for every Table 2 and Results-text value.

location.where: Table 2, 'Insulin ( µU/mL)', Placebo column, rows 0 to 180 min; footnote 1

findings.description: Plasma glucagon before and 120 min after the placebo drink, mean and SE, from the Results text (the other time points are in Figure 3 only). The text prints no n for glucagon; 67 as for Table 2.

location.quote: measuring 38.2 ± 2.3 pg/mL in the placebo group ; after 120 min, glucagon levels increased to 44.3 ± 1.5 pg/mL in the placebo group

left_out.what: Barley dietary fibre (BDF) arm, all values: glucose and insulin curves, Cmax, AUCs and glucagon (Table 2 BDF column; Results 3.3, BDF glucagon 36.8 ± 2.1 and 52.6 ± 2.2 pg/mL). The arm has barley fibre added beyond its grams, so it is not the control meal; the placebo arm is entered instead
Triacylglycerol, placebo arm: 138.0 ± 18.5 mg/dL 'immediately after consumption' falling to 108.3 ± 12.2 mg/dL at 180 min (Results 3.3); the timing of the first value is not clear
PYY, placebo arm: the time course is in Figure 5b only and the text gives no numbers (Results 3.4)
Ghrelin, placebo arm: 713.8 ± 40.4 pg/mL at 60 min (Results 3.4) and the Figure 5a time course; absolute ghrelin is an assay-dependent level
Glucagon at 30, 60 and 180 min, placebo arm (Figure 3 only)
Tmax of glucose (41.0 ± 2.3 min) and insulin (53.8 ± 4.2 min), placebo arm (Table 2): the paper does not say how the time of the maximum was located, and the means are not sampling times
